Teaching machines to see from raw measurements, not images.

I work on single-pixel imaging and image-free sensing: I design optical measurements and train networks that operate directly on the measurement sequence, without first reconstructing an image. A single-pixel camera illuminates a scene with structured patterns and records one value per pattern with a single detector; I study how much a machine can perceive from those values alone. The results hold where conventional approaches struggle: sparse Hadamard patterns keep imaging robust through scattering media, and image-free segmentation maintains near-constant accuracy down to 0.78% sampling. At Politecnico di Milano, I plan to work on time-domain diffuse optical tomography: 3D reconstruction inside scattering media from photon arrival times, from simulation to phantoms. My long-term aim is to enable robotic systems to infer physical parameters and interpret their surroundings directly from raw measurements, guided by physical models.

I am open to research collaborations and internships in computational imaging, image-free sensing and machine perception.

Outside the lab: basketball, fitness and travel.

Selected research

All publications

The Lift Spectrum: How Measurement-to-Space Adaptivity Shapes Robustness in Image-Free Single-Pixel Sensing

Yuyuan Han, Jingwei Li, Xiaoxia Zhang, Long Qiu, Chong Wang, Wenxuan Hao, Jiangyu Han, Xinyu Yao, Yuchen He, Hui Chen, Jianbin Liu, Huaibin Zheng

arXiv preprint · 2026

Image-free sensing moves the hard problem to the 1D-to-2D lift; how adaptive that lift is determines robustness.

  • Near-constant accuracy down to 0.78% sampling
  • Up to +21.7 mIoU at 20 dB over clean-trained reconstruct-then-segment
  • +3.2–9.9 mIoU over the prior image-free method (SPIFS)
  • Runs on a real DMD bench without fine-tuning

Generalized sparse Hadamard single-pixel Imaging

Yuyuan Han, Peng Wu, Hanxiong Xu, Bin Li, Yuchen He, Jianbin Liu, Hui Chen, Huaibin Zheng

Optics Express · 2025

Orthogonal Hadamard patterns with tunable sparsity make single-pixel imaging robust through scattering and noise.

  • Low-order matrices, less memory
  • No training or post-processing
  • Two acquisition modes with theory

Loop differential ghost imaging based on line pattern

Yuyuan Han, Huaibin Zheng, Bin Li, Jingwei Li, Long Qiu, Wenxuan Hao, Zheng Dang, Hui Chen, Jianbin Liu, Yuchen He, Yanyan Liu, Zhuo Xu

Optics Communications · 2025

Line patterns from one-dimensional optical phased arrays break the noise symmetry that ghost-imaging denoising relies on; LDGI overcomes this limitation.

  • Orders-of-magnitude gain over traditional ghost imaging
  • Noise-symmetry metric κs
  • Validated optically

Current directions

  1. Acquisition-aware sensing

    Single-pixel sensing methods that account for acquisition conditions, tested in optical-bench experiments. Manuscript in preparation.

  2. Question answering from measurements

    Exploratory

    Whether a frozen vision–language model can answer questions directly from single-pixel measurements.

  3. Time-domain diffuse optics

    Planned study

    At Politecnico di Milano: 3D reconstruction inside scattering media from photon arrival times, from simulation to phantoms.

Research code

  • STSF-TPLS

    Image-free segmentation from single-pixel measurements with a content-adaptive lift and task-prioritized loss scheduling; code and pretrained weights (PyTorch).

  • Comparison-of-SPI-DLs

    Eight deep architectures and a classical inverse, benchmarked on one shared Hadamard acquisition (PyTorch).

  • SHSI

    Sparse Hadamard single-pixel imaging: pattern generation and reconstruction (MATLAB).

  • LDGI

    Loop differential ghost imaging for line patterns from optical phased arrays (MATLAB).

  • TGIs-Entry

    Reference implementations of traditional, differential and normalized ghost imaging (MATLAB).

  • remote-gpu-trainer

    Open-source agent skill for Claude Code and Codex that runs, verifies and delivers GPU experiments (60+ stars).
